subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept a custom cooperative extra-bootstrap glob walker plus yielded bootstrap hook dispatch as the permanent bounded fix for bootstrap-context stalls, with the documented matching-order and scheduling tradeoffs?
rationale: The patch has no supported mechanical blocker, but it changes compatibility-sensitive prompt/session construction behavior that cannot safely be accepted by automation alone.

options.title: Land after exact-head verification
options.body: Accept the bounded runtime tradeoff, let the current required checks finish for the rebased head, and merge if they remain green.

options.title: Request live channel proof
options.body: Keep the implementation shape but require a redacted current-head embedded-run or channel-latency trace before accepting the compatibility risk.

options.title: Pause for a broader runtime design
options.body: Do not merge this focused mitigation if maintainers prefer worker isolation, caching, or explicit scheduling policy to own the remaining event-loop problem.

recommendation.title: Land after exact-head verification
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded runtime tradeoff, let the current required checks finish for the rebased head, and merge if they remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal spans the hook, bootstrap, and guarded-read contracts whose behavior this PR changes.
